explain.say: Imagine walking for one day over a mountain and finding that the next village speaks a totally different language! In Papua New Guinea that can really happen. It has about 840 languages, more than any other country. Look at the board to see why.

faq.q: Which country has the most languages?
faq.a: Papua New Guinea, with about 840 languages for around 10 million people. Indonesia, with about 700, is second.

faq.q: How do mountains make new languages?
faq.a: When mountains keep groups apart, each group's speech changes in its own way. After thousands of years the changes add up to different languages.
asks: Why do separated people speak differently?

faq.a: Tok Pisin is a shared language used across Papua New Guinea, mixing English words with local grammar. It is one of the country's official languages, with English and Hiri Motu.
asks: What language do people in Papua New Guinea speak?

faq.q: How long have people lived in New Guinea?
faq.a: About 50,000 years. Farmers in the highlands grew crops like taro and bananas thousands of years ago, among the earliest farmers in the world.
asks: When did people arrive in New Guinea?

faq.q: How many people speak each language in Papua New Guinea?
faq.a: Many languages there have only a few thousand speakers, and some just a few hundred.

facts: Papua New Guinea has about 840 living languages, more than any other country.
Tok Pisin, English and Hiri Motu are official languages of Papua New Guinea, along with sign language since 2015.
